title: Android can now securely migrate your logins between password managers
gist: Android now supports on-device transfer of passwords and passkeys between password managers via the Credential Transfer API, shipped through Google Play Services rather than an OS update so it reaches virtually every Google-certified Android device running 8.0 or later. Only Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden and Dashlane have implemented it, and everyone else is still stuck exporting unencrypted CSV files.

insights.claim: Android can now move both passwords and passkeys between managers entirely on-device without creating risky text files, replacing the manual re-entry or unencrypted CSV export that previously locked users into their existing app.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Lowering switching costs in a subscription category increases churn risk for incumbents and makes acquisition-led growth cheaper for challengers.
insights.locator: As longer, more complex passwords have become a necessity

insights.claim: The migration must be initiated from the import option in the destination app, and Google Password Manager's export function still just produces an unencrypted CSV of passwords that can be dumped into any app.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: The secure path is import-driven and one-directional in design, which quietly favors whichever app the user is moving into.
insights.locator: The import option in Google Password Manager

insights.claim: The Android system verifies the user's identity and requires confirmation in the new password manager before completing the move, with both apps installed and credentials synced as prerequisites.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Placing the verification step in the OS rather than the apps makes the platform the trusted broker for credential portability.

themes.theme: Distribution via Play Services and partial ecosystem support

insights.claim: The feature requires no OS update because it is integrated with Google Play Services, working on all devices running Android 8.0 Oreo or higher, and Play Services itself supports back to Android 7.0 Nougat.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Play Services remains Google's mechanism for shipping platform capability past OEM update fragmentation, an underappreciated structural advantage over open Android forks.
insights.locator: This feature doesn’t require an OS update

insights.claim: Password migration should work on virtually every operational Google-certified Android device in the world, giving the feature near-universal reach on day one.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Instant global reach means competitive effects on password-manager market share show up quickly rather than over an OS-upgrade cycle.
insights.quote: password migration should work on virtually every operational Google-certified Android device in the world
insights.locator: This feature doesn’t require an OS update

insights.claim: Only Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden and Dashlane have implemented the Credential Transfer API, and Google says more managers will add support eventually but offers no timeline.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Early API adopters gain a frictionless import path from rivals; managers outside the list face a widening onboarding disadvantage.
insights.locator: If you want to use a password manager that isn’t on the list
